name: Payment Services Regulation (PSR)
impact_assessment: SWD(2023) 231 (executive summary SWD(2023) 232) - joint impact assessment for PSD3 and PSR
evidence_rating: ex-ante only: joint impact assessment with PSD3; fraud baseline statistics; not yet applied
summary: The Payment Services Regulation (shared impact assessment with PSD3) is meant to cut payment scams through payee name checks, fraud data sharing and refunds in some impersonation cases, and to improve open banking; the Commission put the targeted scam losses at about EUR 323 million a year (2020). A political agreement was reached in November 2025 but the rules do not yet apply; reported payment fraud in Europe has since risen to EUR 4.2 billion in 2024.

indicators.objective: Neither PSD3 nor PSR has LFS indicators; the memorandum provides only for a review five years after application (PSR: focus on open banking, fees, fraud liability). PSD3 and PSR share one impact assessment

indicators.indicator: Reduce authorised push payment (social engineering) fraud via IBAN/name check, fraud data sharing, conditional refund liability
indicators.target_or_baseline: Baseline: APP fraud on SEPA credit transfers est. EUR 323m (2020)
indicators.evidence: Baseline worsening, pre-application: EBA-ECB report EEA payment fraud EUR 3.4bn (2022), 3.5bn (2023), 4.2bn (2024); credit transfer fraud EUR 2.2bn in 2024 (+16%), ~85% of losses borne by users. Rules not yet applied (provisional agreement Nov 2025).

indicators.indicator: Better data access interfaces, permission dashboards
indicators.target_or_baseline: One-off cost ~EUR 185-190m (net) for interfaces; up to EUR 47m for dashboards

indicators.indicator: Non-bank PSP access to payment systems and bank accounts; downward pressure on prices
indicators.evidence: Not measured; Settlement Finality Directive access change partly delivered via the Instant Payments Regulation (2024).

literature.citation: European Commission (2023), Impact Assessment accompanying the proposals for a Payment Services Regulation and a Payment Services Directive (PSD3), SWD(2023) 231 (executive summary SWD(2023) 232) - joint impact assessment for PSD3 and PSR
literature.title: Impact Assessment accompanying the proposals for a Payment Services Regulation and a Payment Services Directive (PSD3)
literature.venue: SWD(2023) 231 (executive summary SWD(2023) 232) - joint impact assessment for PSD3 and PSR
literature.outcomes: fraud; open banking; competition; compliance costs
literature.headline: Main benefit: reduction of social engineering fraud (APP fraud on SEPA credit transfers estimated at EUR 323m a year in 2020); more open banking innovation, more bank/non-bank competition. Costs: IBAN/name check for 1,200-1,300 PSPs (~EUR 50m one-off), permission dashboards up to EUR 47m, interface upgrades ~EUR 185m one-off offset by savings
literature.summary_plain: The Commission expected the payments package to cut fraud in which customers are tricked into paying scammers (put at about EUR 323 million a year) and to boost open banking, at one-off costs of a few hundred million euros.
literature.verified: executive summary read; full text searched

literature.citation: European Commission (2023), Report on the review of Directive 2015/2366/EU on payment services (PSD2), COM(2023) 365
literature.title: Report on the review of Directive 2015/2366/EU on payment services (PSD2)
literature.headline: PSD2 objectives only partly achieved: strong customer authentication cut fraud on authenticated payments, but social engineering fraud persists and open banking is hampered by inadequate interfaces
literature.summary_plain: The Commission's review of the previous payments directive found that strong authentication cut card fraud but scams and poor bank data interfaces remained problems.

literature.citation: European Banking Authority & European Central Bank (2025), 2025 Report on payment fraud, EBA-ECB joint report, 15 December 2025
literature.authors: European Banking Authority & European Central Bank
literature.title: 2025 Report on payment fraud
literature.headline: EEA payment fraud EUR 3.4bn (2022), 3.5bn (2023), 4.2bn (2024); credit transfer fraud EUR 2.2bn in 2024 (+16%), ~85% borne by users, mainly manipulation scams; SCA still effective against fraud it targets
literature.summary_plain: Payment fraud in Europe rose to EUR 4.2 billion in 2024, with customers bearing most losses from scams - the baseline the new rules aim to improve.
